target: Decide chi(G(n,7)) for the uniformly random 7-regular graph (n even, n -> infinity): prove chi = 4 asymptotically almost surely, or isolate the exact failing dependency of the proposed route.

primary_attestation.kpw: Kemkes, Perez-Gimenez, Wormald, arXiv:0812.2937v1 (Adv. Math. 2010), Theorem 1 p.3: 'let k be the smallest integer such that d < 2(k - 1) log(k - 1). Then the chromatic number of G_{n,d} is a.a.s. k - 1 or k.' At d = 7 this gives k = 5, i.e. chi in {4,5}; the exact-value clause needs d > (2k-3)log(k-1) = 7 log 4 and does not apply. Parent-pinned copy: review/colour7-parent-source-screen-v1/kpw0812.2937v1.pdf (sha256 recorded in that manifest).
primary_attestation.acg: Ayre, Coja-Oghlan, Greenhill, arXiv:1812.09691v4 (19 Oct 2021), Table 1: q = 4 has d_{q,smm} = 6 (the value up to which the second-moment theorem (1.2) implies chi(G(n,d)) <= q) and d_q = 10; q = 3 has d_q = 6. Hence d = 7, 8, 9 are undetermined in that table. Parent-pinned copy and layout text: review/colour7-parent-source-screen-v2/ (manifest).
primary_attestation.secondary: Shi-Wormald, Combin. Probab. Comput. 16 (2007) abstract: chromatic number '{4, 5} for d = 7, 8, 9' (abstract mirror only; body not read).

proposed_route_untrusted: Scout Colour7Screen (read-only, 2026-10-17, agent://Colour7Screen): KPW use their hypothesis d < 2(k-1)log(k-1) only for k^2-2k-d+2 > 0 (here 3 > 0) and the global bound (3.15) from Achlioptas-Naor Theorem 7/(5). The Achlioptas-Naor proof (Annals 162 (2005), eq. (12) p.1348, with Theorem 9) actually yields Theorem 7 for every c <= (k-1)^3 log(k-1)/(k(k-2)); at k = 4 this is (27/8) ln 3 = 3.7078 > 7/2 = d/2. Equivalently the per-row inequality D(p||U_4) >= (3/2) ln 3 (sum p_i^2 - 1/4) gives the needed quadratic decay of phi(M) = -(1/4) sum m ln m + (d/2) ln(1/2 + sum m^2/16) on 4x4 doubly stochastic M for d < (27/4) ln 3 = 7.4156. The lower bound chi >= 4 is the first-moment non-3-colourability: ln 3 + (7/2) ln(2/3) < 0. Every step is [INFERENCE] until proved and checked.

acceptance.proof: A self-contained written proof of chi(G(n,7)) = 4 a.a.s. that states each imported theorem with exact hypotheses and verifies them at (k,d) = (4,7): the sharpened Achlioptas-Naor inequality with an explicit strictly positive quadratic-decay constant on the Birkhoff polytope; every use of the d-hypothesis in KPW Sections 2-4 (including Proposition 2(b), the small-subgraph-conditioning ratio, the n not divisible by 4 extension and Theorem 10); and the lower bound. All numeric inequalities rigorously verified with exact rational bounds or interval arithmetic.
acceptance.refutation_of_route: An exact point or rigorous enclosure showing the needed global bound fails, or a hypothesis of a cited step that genuinely fails at d = 7; this would only stop the route, not answer chi.
acceptance.insufficient: Numerical multistart searches, a restatement of KPW, or importing (3.15) without proving it at d = 7.

controls: Reproduce KPW's original threshold arithmetic (k=4 needs d < 6 ln 3 = 6.59); show the same sharpened argument does not reach d = 8 (exhibit a doubly stochastic M with phi_8(M) > phi_8(J/4), rigorously enclosed); reproduce chi(G_{n,6}) = 4 and the known 3-colourability failure for d >= 6 as arithmetic controls.
priority_kill_check: Before claiming openness, search the Kemkes 2008 Waterloo thesis, Achlioptas-Moore 2004 (random regular graphs), Shi-Wormald 2007, works citing Achlioptas-Naor that state the (k-1)^3 log(k-1)/(k(k-2)) constant, and 2021-2026 chromatic-number papers. Report dated misses and access holes; a miss is not novelty.
